entry.content:
OnCo · weekly issue

OnCo weekly, 2026-11-17

1524 changelog entries, 5 regulatory events, 2 upcoming dates, 724 corrections. Generated from the corpus; every item links to its page and, through it, to the primary source. Not medical advice.

What changed this week

New pages, new data and fixes, from the changelog.

  • 17 November 2026: Second accuracy pass on live country pages, continued: corrections to eighteen more pages, among them Haiti, Senegal, Slovenia, Mali, Papua New Guinea, Burkina Faso, Costa Rica, Paraguay, Belgium, Cuba, Czechia, Greece and Portugal, each claim read against its source again
  • 17 November 2026: Second accuracy pass on live country pages: corrections to 53 pages after every claim was read against its source again, including what the IAEA radiotherapy directory lists for 36 countries, WHO's HPV vaccination data where pages had said there was none, and sources pages had called unreadable that do answer
  • 17 November 2026: The first weekly gap fill read from FDA sources lands, each fact checked against the FDA list and device records: the Guardant360 Liquid CDx blood test approved on 19 May 2026 with its seven drug pairings, and four companion tests linked to the biomarkers they read
  • 17 November 2026: More of the graph is joined up: 1,251 confirmed links between people and the trials whose papers they wrote, matched by ORCID or full name and affiliation; who pays for 21 tests in the US and UK, from Medicare national coverage decisions and NICE guidance; fifty warning-card lines now name the protocol that manages them; and eight wrong side-effect links are removed
  • 17 November 2026: Twenty-two more care protocols close the gaps in the census, among them stoma care, drain care at home, transplant conditioning, veno-occlusive disease, lung biopsy, intrathecal chemotherapy in children, end-of-life care for children, advance care planning and stopping smoking after a diagnosis; 212 protocols in all, with a table of what is covered and what is still open
  • 17 November 2026: Shasqi in depth: its clinical programme SQ3370, its trial and the click-activated chemistry behind it, from the company's own pages, the registry and the published papers; the weekly gap-fill job gets the tools it needs to read its allowed sources; and the command-line tool and MCP server are rebuilt to know about care protocols
  • 17 November 2026: A contributor's education work arrives, 215 new records on biomarkers, immune tests, specimens, RNA and clinical evidence, with every source checked; and a backlog of corrections lands: new FDA approvals including pimicotinib, four generic icons removed from logos, mislabelled trials fixed, radiotherapy counts for Madagascar and Angola, the two Cuban lung cancer vaccines, and 33 records renamed for their subject
  • 17 November 2026: chore: draft change proposals that need review (#441)
  • 17 November 2026: chore: EU regional rows read from the EMA register pages (#440)
  • 17 November 2026: chore: draft records for gaps in the freshness issue, for review
  • 16 November 2026: CIMAvax-EGF: one-line description shortened to fit, facts unchanged
  • 16 November 2026: Second accuracy pass, batch four: Belgium, Cuba, Czechia, Greece, Portugal, Hungary, Belarus and Bulgaria
  • 16 November 2026: Second accuracy pass on the last eight live country pages (wave 11): Haiti, Senegal, Slovenia, Mali, Papua New Guinea, Burkina Faso, Costa Rica and Paraguay
  • 16 November 2026: Second accuracy pass on live country pages: corrections to 53 pages after every claim was read against its source again, including what the IAEA radiotherapy directory lists for 36 countries, WHO's HPV vaccination data where pages had said there was none, and sources pages had called unreadable that do answer
  • 16 November 2026: Casablanca cancer centre: one-line description shortened to fit, with the fuller wording kept in the summary
  • 16 November 2026: Second accuracy pass, batch three: Venezuela, Sri Lanka, Syria, Kazakhstan, Cambodia, Ecuador, Zimbabwe, Chile and Tunisia, and HPV vaccination figures re-read on the earlier pages
  • 16 November 2026: Second accuracy pass, batch two: Ghana, Saudi Arabia, Peru and Nepal, and the IAEA radiotherapy directory read for all sixteen pages checked so far
  • 16 November 2026: Second accuracy pass on twelve live country pages: DR Congo, Tanzania, Kenya, Myanmar, Sudan, Uganda, Iraq, Afghanistan, Yemen, Morocco, Angola and Uzbekistan
  • 16 November 2026: Second accuracy pass on twelve more live country pages (wave 10): Chad, Lebanon, Bolivia, Zambia, Puerto Rico, Uruguay, Lithuania, Niger, Cameroon, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Bosnia and Herzegovina

  • 16 November 2026: Second accuracy pass on ten live country pages (wave 12): Guinea, Honduras, Armenia, Somalia, El Salvador, Jordan, Rwanda, Moldova, Latvia and Panama
  • 16 November 2026: The first weekly gap fill read from FDA sources lands, each fact checked against the FDA list and device records: the Guardant360 Liquid CDx blood test approved on 19 May 2026 with its seven drug pairings, and four companion tests linked to the biomarkers they read
  • 16 November 2026: Review of the 17 November gap fill: Guardant360 Liquid CDx gets a row in the tests box of the eight readouts it measures, the BRACAnalysis CDx row on the prostate HRR readout says it covers BRCA1 and BRCA2 only, the FDA companion diagnostic list is cited at its new address, and the gap audit no longer reads the SP142 and SP263 PD-L1 assays as one product
  • 16 November 2026: More of the graph is joined up: 1,251 confirmed links between people and the trials whose papers they wrote, matched by ORCID or full name and affiliation; who pays for 21 tests in the US and UK, from Medicare national coverage decisions and NICE guidance; fifty warning-card lines now name the protocol that manages them; and eight wrong side-effect links are removed
  • 16 November 2026: Twenty-two more care protocols close the gaps in the census, among them stoma care, drain care at home, transplant conditioning, veno-occlusive disease, lung biopsy, intrathecal chemotherapy in children, end-of-life care for children, advance care planning and stopping smoking after a diagnosis; 212 protocols in all, with a table of what is covered and what is still open
  • 16 November 2026: Shasqi in depth: its clinical programme SQ3370, its trial and the click-activated chemistry behind it, from the company's own pages, the registry and the published papers; the weekly gap-fill job gets the tools it needs to read its allowed sources; and the command-line tool and MCP server are rebuilt to know about care protocols

  • 16 November 2026: The National Cancer Institute and Cancer Research UK records carry their abbreviations as aliases
  • 16 November 2026: Fifty warning-card lines name the protocol that manages them
  • 16 November 2026: The scalp cooling record says in its first line what the cap is for, preventing or reducing hair loss, so a question about hair loss still finds it beside the longer care protocol
  • 16 November 2026: The coverage table records that Europe PMC holds no open copy of the two interventional radiology standards on blood thinners before a biopsy, so that row stays open
  • 16 November 2026: A contributor's education work arrives, 215 new records on biomarkers, immune tests, specimens, RNA and clinical evidence, with every source checked; and a backlog of corrections lands: new FDA approvals including pimicotinib, four generic icons removed from logos, mislabelled trials fixed, radiotherapy counts for Madagascar and Angola, the two Cuban lung cancer vaccines, and 33 records renamed for their subject
  • 16 November 2026: Protocols page weight: the live page weighs 157,107 bytes, over the 155,000 ceiling, so the ceiling stays and the note says so
  • 16 November 2026: The onco-cc and onco-mcp packages go to 0.1.1, so a rebuild that knows the protocol kind can be published
  • 16 November 2026: The recorded Ask rubric is the figure measured after merging main: 0.6765
  • 16 November 2026: The gap-fill workflow installs bubblewrap and socat, so the fetch tool can start inside the command sandbox
  • 16 November 2026: Evidence keeps its scope: conjugate payload pages show each measurement with the exact chemical form it was made on and how it was tested, drug pages show what a conjugate is made of, assay approvals say who authorised what and for which use, and a missing measurement reads as a gap in our records and not as a no; a contributor's work, reviewed and put into plain language
  • 16 November 2026: Shasqi in depth: its one clinical programme SQ3370 with the stopped phase 1/2a trial and its results, the click-activated prodrug technology, seven resolved papers, and a company record corrected to say the trial was terminated and carrying sourced leadership, financing and grants
  • 16 November 2026: The plain-language summaries of the new care protocols and their upgrade ideas are tightened to the 400-character limit every record keeps
  • 16 November 2026: The glossary size recorded for the Wikipedia-link gauge is brought up to the live count of 1,685 terms
  • 16 November 2026: Giredestrant's United States row now records its approval; the two Cuban vaccines are filed as established, as nimotuzumab is, and their trial papers link to them; stale trial-site and country entries removed
  • 16 November 2026: The two registrations of the PILDI colon surgery trial stay as two records for now, each saying they are one study: merging them adds a redirect line that waits for the owner's approval
  • 16 November 2026: Corrections log: the sixteen faults fixed from the review backlog on 16 November 2026, each with its source
  • 16 November 2026: Thirty-three paper records named as questions or how-sentences are renamed for their subject, so a record's name no longer competes with the questions readers ask; papers whose published title is itself a question keep it
  • 16 November 2026: The cancer blood clot treatment protocol now links enoxaparin and dalteparin, the two heparins its own guideline names; twelve Newsweek-ranked hospitals whose sites still refuse a script stay unwritten and are named
  • 16 November 2026: CIMAvax-EGF and racotumomab, Cuba's two registered lung cancer vaccines, get product pages written from the Cuban regulator's registration entries and the two randomised trials
  • 16 November 2026: Nine records corrected from their sources: Angola's cancer institute no longer shows a paper's DOI as its website; the University of Puerto Rico cancer centre is filed under Puerto Rico; the technology tags on King Hussein Cancer Center and King Faisal Specialist Hospital each rest on a page of the hospital's own, and one that had none is removed; IPO Lisboa no longer claims a regional registry that the 2017 law folded into the national one; the Senegal and Nigeria breast cancer cohort's mean age is given for the 378 women it describes; and the Madagascar, Angola and Somalia pages carry the IAEA's radiotherapy counts and the Somali ministry's statement that the country has no medicines regulator yet
  • 16 November 2026: ESPAC-4 no longer shows ESPAC-3's sites, sponsor and dates: the ISRCTN record lists a ClinicalTrials.gov number that belongs to ESPAC-3, the fetcher now refuses that cross-reference, and the Greek and Hungarian pages name ESPAC-3 as the trial that ran there; SIRveNIB's own registration (NCT01135056), publication and result join SARAH's on their shared record
  • 16 November 2026: Four trial records corrected against ClinicalTrials.gov: a children's bladder-drug trial that was never a cancer trial is removed with its false links to childhood cancers and to the CIC gene; two Cushing's disease trials now say what they tested and why they sit under pituitary tumours; the PILDI colon surgery trial, held twice under two registration numbers, is one record; and the vulvar electrochemotherapy study carries the registry's own entry (no phase, status unknown, 20 participants) in place of phase 2 and recruiting
  • 16 November 2026: Four records lose a web host's stock icon shown as their logo (Apmonia Therapeutics, Loki Therapeutics, Cansera, Japan Psycho-Oncology Society), and the logo fetcher now refuses any new file that is byte-for-byte a known generic icon: the WordPress and Vercel defaults, the HostGator mascot, the European Commission emblem and grey placeholders
  • 16 November 2026: FDA approval notices are counted once each: the fetcher now identifies a notice by its date and title, so FDA's move of the notices to a new address no longer doubles the list, and the refreshed list brings the four approvals of 5 to 16 November 2026 (subcutaneous amivantamab in head and neck cancer, pimicotinib, durvalumab with enfortumab vedotin, giredestrant) onto their records with the FDA's own words
  • 16 November 2026: Twenty-two new care protocols close gaps the census found, among them stoma care, drain care at home, transplant conditioning, veno-occlusive disease, children's central lines and end of life care, advance care planning and ReSPECT; three existing protocols gain hair care during scalp cooling and label dose rules for skin reactions
  • 16 November 2026: A coverage table places all 251 subjects of the care protocol census against the protocols OnCo holds: 182 had their own record, 51 were covered inside another, and 18 were not covered
  • 16 November 2026: Ask's retrieval measurement is recorded after the contributor batch: recall 0.4365 against a floor of 0.4293, floors unchanged
  • 16 November 2026: Translated summaries for pathological complete response and radiotherapy follow their rewritten English text, and two Chinese summaries that no longer match are withdrawn
  • 16 November 2026: chore: draft records for gaps in the freshness issue, for review
  • 16 November 2026: Teaching records now cite the primary papers and guidance only: 22 links to the contributor's own teaching notes are removed, 66 placeholder source labels carry their paper's real title, and the short definition of biomarker returns to its plainer wording
  • 16 November 2026: Payload, drug and test pages say what was measured in words a patient can follow
  • 16 November 2026: The RAS pathway page keeps its plain explanation, and a sourced link no longer switches off the drug highlighting
  • 16 November 2026: Teaching concepts across biology, tests, treatments and trial evidence get a contributor's audit: 137 new records and about 500 revised ones, each with its sources, and the corrections they record
  • 16 November 2026: Weekly gap-fill automation, with the model's fetching limited to an allow-list of regulators, registries and societies
  • 16 November 2026: Antibody-drug conjugate payloads get deeper coverage from a contributor: 34 new records and 31 supplemented ones that keep free drugs, attached linker-drugs and released forms apart, each measurement with its experiment and source
  • 16 November 2026: Glossary links now respect capitals, so ordinary words such as platinum, select, open and decision no longer link to trials and acronyms that share their spelling, about twelve thousand false links fewer; with the weekly refresh of trial counts, universe lists, logos, the fact check and two EU register rows
  • 16 November 2026: Names with a digit link in any case again, and the ordinary words "verify" and "alliance" stop linking
  • 16 November 2026: Eighty more countries get deep dives researched by agents and checked claim by claim by a second agent, the menu shows one Countries entry instead of a line per country, Ask reads first any medicine a question names by name or brand, and the ivonescimab record now states that the FDA issued a complete response letter, announced on 15 November 2026
  • 16 November 2026: Names in capitals of any length link only where written in capitals, and bracket qualifiers in record names stop linking ordinary words
  • 16 November 2026: Nine source links in the immune-concepts round now name the paper instead of showing only a PubMed number
  • 16 November 2026: Ivonescimab: the FDA issued a complete response letter on the US application, announced 15 November 2026
  • 16 November 2026: Vedolizumab gets its EU approval row, read from the EMA register, and one RP-6306 trial loses a subtype link its text does not support

  • 2026-11-16 · Giredestrant · approval (US): FDA approved giredestrant (Wilserdly, Genentech, Inc.), an oral estrogen receptor antagonist, in combination with everolimus for the treatment of adults with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, estrogen receptor 1 ( ESR1) -mutated locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, as detected by an FDA-authorized test, whose disease has recurred during or after completion of endocrine-based adjuvant therapy, or has progressed on at least one endocrine-based regimen in the metastatic setting. source

  • 2026-11-14 · Ivonescimab · pdufa (US): PDUFA target date source
  • 2026-11-13 · Durvalumab · approval (US): FDA approved durvalumab (Imfinzi, AstraZeneca) in combination with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv as neoadjuvant treatment, followed by single agent durvalumab as adjuvant treatment after radical cystectomy, for the treatment of adult patients with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are ineligible for or who have refused cisplatin based chemotherapy. source
  • 2026-11-10 · Pimicotinib · approval (US): FDA approved pimicotinib (Pimjetmi, EMD Serono, Inc.), a kinase inhibitor, for adults with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) for which surgical resection may cause worsening functional limitation or severe morbidity.   • 2026-11-16 · Mali country page: The GLOBOCAN note said "Mortality has no national source". The fact sheet gives SURVCAN as the country-specific mortality source. (Second accuracy pass; IARC GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet for Mali, PDF text) · Now says the fact sheet gives SURVCAN as the country-specific source, with deaths estimated from incidence using modelled mortality-to-incidence ratios.
  • 2026-11-16 · Mali country page: The table note said "Mali has no national cancer registry and no national death data on cancer", an absence no cited source states. (Second accuracy pass; WHO cancer country profile 2020 for Mali, PDF text) · Replaced with what WHO's profile says: mortality registration "No coverage" for 2007 to 2016, and mortality estimates not based on any national data on deaths from noncommunicable diseases.
  • 2026-11-16 · Mali country page: The description, lede, a card title and the registry record said the Bamako registry had "counted cancers since 1986" or been "running since 1986". The registry's page says it was created in 1986; the registry paper dates its data from 1987. (Second accuracy pass; African Cancer Registry Network member page (HTML text) and Amadou et al. 2022 abstract through Europe PMC) · Reworded to "created in 1986", with data from 1987.
  • 2026-11-16 · Mali country page: The radiotherapy card's title and the lede stated as fact that Mali has one radiotherapy centre, and dated the IAEA directory reading 11 November 2026. (Second accuracy pass; IAEA DIRAC public equipment feed, raw JSON fetched 16 November 2026) · Now a dated listing: the directory, read on 16 November 2026, lists one centre, the Hôpital du Mali Radiotherapy Center in Bamako (entry last updated 2026), with two linear accelerators, no cobalt-60 unit and no brachytherapy. The per-population figure is marked as OnCo's arithmetic.
  • 2026-11-16 · Mali country page: The free chemotherapy card said the DPM "validates" the hospital's needs and "the Ministry orders", and that "women interviewed in 2024" described free care as incomplete. The paper says the DPM passes the validated needs to the Ministry's finance directorate; 2024 is the interview study's publication year. (Second accuracy pass; Ballo et al., Health Sciences and Disease 2022, PDF text; Schantz et al. 2024 abstract through Europe PMC) · Supply chain reworded to the paper's steps; the sentence now reads "An interview study published in 2024".
  • 2026-11-16 · Mali country page: The record for the 2026 cervical cancer cohort at Gabriel Touré carried a shortened title and concluded that "most women with cervical cancer in Mali are diagnosed too late for cure" from one hospital's cohort. The liver cancer paper's "first such decrease in Africa" was stated as fact. (Second accuracy pass; abstracts of DOI 10.1155/ogi/9966827 and 10.4254/wjh.v14.i9.1767 through Europe PMC) · Published title restored; the conclusion is limited to the referral hospital; the "first" is attributed to the authors.
  • 2026-11-16 · Mali country page: The Ministry's record called it the ministry "for health and social protection", listed free anticancer medicines as supplied "to public hospitals", and CHU du Point G's record said it hosts "the national cancer registry". (Second accuracy pass; Ministry of Health and Social Development news pages, the Health Sciences and Disease paper and the African Cancer Registry Network page, raw text) · Now "health and social development"; the supply is described as documented at CHU du Point G; the registry is called the Bamako cancer registry.
  • 2026-11-16 · Papua New Guinea country page: The HPV card said WHO's coverage data "held no HPV rows for Papua New Guinea ... so there is no coverage figure yet". The query had used a narrow antigen filter. (Second accuracy pass; WHO immunisation coverage rows for PNG fetched as raw JSON with the broad HPV filter on 16 November 2026) · Now says the data holds 44 HPV rows for 2018 to 2025 (final-dose rows for girls and boys from 2018, first-dose rows from 2023), none with a dose count or coverage value, and has no figure yet for the programme begun in 2026; the causal "so" is gone and the link uses the broad filter.
  • 2026-11-16 · Papua New Guinea country page: The regulator card said the memorandum with Australia ran to 31 March 2021 and that the TGA offered "up to five" samples a year. (Second accuracy pass; the scanned memorandum on the National Department of Health site, read by OCR) · Now says the memorandum ran until 1 June 2021 and that the TGA undertook to test five samples in each Australian financial year until 31 March 2021.
  • 2026-11-16 · Papua New Guinea country page: The lede said IARC has no national incidence data "so" the figures are a model, called the registry "set up in the 1980s", and said radiotherapy "is given in one place" without a source or date. (Second accuracy pass; IARC GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet (PDF text), National Cancer Control Policy 2015 (PDF text), IAEA directory feed saved 16 November 2026) · Each statement is now given as its source gives it: the fact sheet lists no country-specific incidence data and models the figures; the policy says a registry was in place in the 1980s; IAEA's directory lists one centre.
  • 2026-11-16 · Papua New Guinea country page: The HPV card said the 2015 policy "had only proposed exploring the vaccine's feasibility", and that vaccination was "starting" in two provinces in November 2026. (Second accuracy pass; National Cancer Control Policy 2015 (PDF text) and WHO's release of 8 September 2026 (page text)) · Now says the policy listed introducing HPV vaccination among its objectives with a strategy to explore feasibility, and that the first phase was due to begin in November 2026.
  • 2026-11-16 · Papua New Guinea country page: The radiotherapy card gave 2015 statements as current (Port Moresby General Hospital "gives chemotherapy but not radiotherapy"), said the policy "proposed" a second centre, and described the IAEA entry with "one X-ray therapy unit", read on 11 November. (Second accuracy pass; National Cancer Control Policy 2015 (PDF text) and IAEA's directory feed saved 16 November 2026) · The 2015 statements are attributed to the policy, which said it would consider a second centre; the IAEA listing is restated from the feed (two cobalt-60 units, no linear accelerator, one low-dose-rate remote afterloading brachytherapy unit, one X-ray generator, entry last updated 2024) with a note that a directory can lag.
  • 2026-11-16 · Papua New Guinea country page: The admissions table and the registry card credited the 28%, 15%, 9% and 9% shares to the National Health Information System's admissions, and said a childhood cancer registry "has been developed" at Port Moresby General Hospital. (Second accuracy pass; National Cancer Control Policy 2015, section 3.1 (PDF text) and the abstract of Raj et al. 2025 through Europe PMC) · The shares are given as the policy's own recalculation, with the section's credit to the information system noted; the registry sentence now says the partnership with SIOP Oceania has helped develop a registry.
  • 2026-11-16 · Papua New Guinea country page: The Port Moresby General Hospital record said the 2015 policy describes it as the national referral hospital; the survival gap card said there is no national survival estimate because there is no working registry, and predicted when WHO coverage figures would come. (Second accuracy pass; National Cancer Control Policy 2015 (PDF text)) · The record no longer credits that description to the policy; the gap card says OnCo found no survival estimate and that the policy said population-based data did not exist, and the prediction is removed.
  • 2026-11-16 · Burkina Faso country page: The lede said "Burkina Faso has no cancer registry whose figures IARC can use, so its national cancer figures are estimates", the description said the estimate was "made without a national incidence source", and a card was titled "No registry incidence figures that IARC can use". WHO's 2020 cancer country profile records a population-based cancer registry for 2019, and WHO's survey rows answer yes for 2019 and 2021; IARC's fact sheet only leaves its country-specific incidence source blank and gives no cause. (Second accuracy pass; WHO cancer country profile 2020 (PDF text), WHO Global Health Observatory rows NCD_CCS_PBCR and NCD_CCS_CancerRegNational (API JSON), IARC GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet (PDF text)) · Reworded to what each source says: IARC names no Burkinabè incidence source; WHO recorded a population-based registry in 2019 and 2021 (no in 2013, 2015 and 2017) without naming it; OnCo found no published figures from one. The causal wording is gone.
  • 2026-11-16 · Burkina Faso country page: A gap card said WHO's 2020 cancer country profile for Burkina Faso "could not be reached" and that its indicators were therefore missing. The profile is published at a different file name (cancer-bfa-2020.pdf) and answers. (Second accuracy pass; WHO cancer country profile 2020, Burkina Faso (PDF text)) · The gap card now says what the profile records (a population-based registry for 2019, no coverage for mortality registration in 2007 to 2016, no external beam radiotherapy in 2019, visual inspection screening, staff only as rates per 10,000 cancer patients) and that its indicators predate the Bogodogo radiotherapy centre; the link points to the working file.
  • 2026-11-16 · Burkina Faso country page: The HPV card said WHO's coverage rows "begin in 2022" and linked a narrow query; it also called the 2014 and 2015 vaccination in two districts "pilot campaigns", a word the Ministry's page does not use. (Second accuracy pass; WHO immunisation data queried with the broad HPV filter (API JSON), Ministry of Health page of 10 February 2021 (Internet Archive capture, raw HTML)) · The card now says the rows run from 2010 with no values before 2022, keeps WHO's estimates (first dose 70%, 96%, 99%, 95% for 2022 to 2025), adds the country's own administrative reports (95.78% in 2023, 103.81% in 2024, 149.59% in 2025), and says "a vaccination campaign in two health districts". The link uses the broad filter.
  • 2026-11-16 · Burkina Faso country page: The screening card named the organiser of the 2023 breast screening campaign as the "Coalition Burkinabè Contre le Cancer" and said the campaign would assess capacity for "breast ultrasound and mammography"; the Ministry's page says "coalition burkinabè de lutte contre le cancer (COBUCAN)" and "écho-mammographies". (Second accuracy pass; Ministry of Health page of 24 April 2023 (Internet Archive capture, raw HTML)) · Reworded to "the Burkinabè coalition against cancer (COBUCAN)" and "breast imaging (écho-mammographies in the Ministry's report)".
  • 2026-11-16 · Burkina Faso country page: The radiotherapy card said IAEA's directory recorded "no CT simulator" and described "megavoltage machines"; the directory's columns for CT, simulators and TPS are zero and undefined. The Faso FDA card said "patients can report a side effect through the Med Safety app", where the regulator's page only links to the app. The CHU de Bogodogo record said IAEA gave "support for licensing"; the 2019 statement says assistance for institutional capacity building. (Second accuracy pass; IAEA DIRAC public feed (JSON saved 16 November 2026), Faso FDA presentation page (raw HTML), Burkina Faso statement to the IAEA General Conference 2019 (PDF text)) · The directory is now quoted by its plain columns, with the centre name as the feed spells it, the read date and the 2025 entry year; the Faso FDA card says its site links to Med Safety; the Bogodogo record says IAEA assistance for institutional capacity building.
  • 2026-11-16 · Burkina Faso country page: The trials card said only that a ClinicalTrials.gov search "may find" Burkinabè studies and gave no size for OnCo's own data. (Second accuracy pass; src/data/trial-participation.ts recount and the ClinicalTrials.gov API (JSON)) · The card now gives the denominators (5,897 trial records, 5,578 listing countries, none listing Burkina Faso) and says a ClinicalTrials.gov search on 16 November 2026 returned seven studies, one of them a malaria study.
  • 2026-11-16 · Costa Rica country page: The lede said IARC "builds its estimate" on the national registry kept since 1976, and a table note said IARC's figure is above the registry's counts because it projects them forward. IARC's fact sheet names no registry and gives no such cause. (Second accuracy pass; IARC GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet for Costa Rica, PDF text) · The lede now says IARC's estimate is projected from national registry and mortality data, and the note states IARC's method and the registry's lower, preliminary counts separately.
  • 2026-11-16 · Costa Rica country page: The page said WHO records 57% of boys vaccinated against HPV in 2025, with no qualifier, and linked WHO's data with a narrow filter that hides the rows the country reported. (Second accuracy pass; WHO immunisation data API, raw JSON, queried with contains(ANTIGEN,'HPV')) · The card now gives both rows: WHO's programme coverage of 57% first dose and 57% last dose for boys in 2025, and the administrative row of 96.4% first dose (35,553 doses for 36,881 boys), and says the first-dose figure is uncertain. The link uses the broad filter. The title no longer attributes the 2021 fall to the pandemic.
  • 2026-11-16 · Costa Rica country page: The radiotherapy card called two hospitals public and three centres private and dated its reading 11 November 2026; the IAEA directory has no ownership field. (Second accuracy pass; IAEA DIRAC public feed, raw JSON saved 16 November 2026 (Costa Rica's five rows are filed under country code CS)) · The card states what the directory lists, read on 16 November 2026: five centres, 12 linear accelerators, no cobalt-60 unit, brachytherapy only at Hospital México (one iridium-192 unit), entries last updated 2021 to 2026, with a note that the 2021 entry may be out of date. The public and private labels are removed.
  • 2026-11-16 · Costa Rica country page: The description and a card title said the Guanacaste trials showed one HPV vaccine dose "is enough", and the card placed two decades of trials in Guanacaste. The ESCUDDO abstract reports noninferiority against HPV 16 and 18 infection, and the Costa Rica Vaccine Trial and PRISMA abstracts say only Costa Rica. (Second accuracy pass; Europe PMC abstracts for PubMed 41337735, 33271093 and DOI 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129236, and the ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT03180034) · The text now says ESCUDDO, based in Liberia in Guanacaste, found one dose protects against HPV 16 and 18 infection as well as two, and that the trials have run in Costa Rica since 2004.
  • 2026-11-16 · Costa Rica country page: The trials card said OnCo's data list Costa Rican sites in 23 cancer trials, "almost all" company trials for six cancers. The data list Costa Rica in 24 records, one of them a Cushing's disease trial, and all are company-sponsored. (Second accuracy pass; recount of src/data/trial-participation.ts) · The card now says 24 of 5,897 trial records list Costa Rica, 23 of them cancer trials, all sponsored by international companies, and that they also cover bladder cancer, lymphoma and three extension studies.
  • 2026-11-16 · Costa Rica country page: Several statements went beyond the national cancer plan: the workforce table was credited to a 2022 follow-up of the 2014 imPACT review, the screening register was said to be planned because results are not collected in one system, HPV coverage was said to come from the Ministry's own data, and 4,296 people were said to be seen by multidisciplinary teams "in 2021". (Second accuracy pass; Plan Nacional para el Control del Cáncer 2024-2030, PDF text) · The workforce table is described as a 2021 count sourced to a Ministry report of 2022; the register as a new project with no baseline; the data-source phrase is removed; the multidisciplinary figure reads "by 2021"; the EBAIS and health-area counts are attributed to the 2015 CCSS plan the document cites.
  • 2026-11-16 · Costa Rica country page: The courts card and the Loaiza paper record said "fewer rulings" granted experimental medicines after 2014; the study reports that the percentage of such rulings declined, not their number. The ACIB-FUNIN record said staff were lent "in 2023", a year the Ministry's release does not give. (Second accuracy pass; Europe PMC full text of PMC6039739 and the Ministry of Health release of 15 December 2023) · Both now say "a smaller share of rulings", and the ACIB-FUNIN record reports what the Ministry said in December 2023.
  • 2026-11-16 · Paraguay country page: The lede and the registry card said Paraguay "has no population-based cancer registry that IARC can use, so" its incidence is modelled, and that it "has no cancer registry whose figures IARC uses". No source gives a cause, and WHO's latest row says a registry exists. (Second accuracy pass; IARC GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet PDF text ("Country-specific data source: No data") and WHO Global Health Observatory JSON rows NCD_CCS_CancerRegNational and NCD_CCS_PBCR for PRY) · Now states IARC's "No data" without a cause, and WHO's rows for "Existence of population-based cancer registry": "No" for 2013, 2015, 2017 and 2019, "Yes" for 2021, with both rows linked
  • 2026-11-16 · Paraguay country page: The HPV card, its title and the page description said coverage for girls "fell from about 80% to 42%" without naming the measure; the link queried only WHO's programme-coverage rows (Second accuracy pass; WHO immunisation data JSON for PRY with every HPV antigen (174 rows)) · Named as WHO's yearly programme coverage; added WHO's by-age-15 first-dose estimate (98% in 2017, 78% in 2020, 77% in 2025), the 24% last-dose figure for 2023 and Paraguay's own reported 2025 figures (41.76% girls, 38.53% boys); link widened to all HPV rows
  • 2026-11-16 · Paraguay country page: The radiotherapy card called the directory's count "11 radiotherapy machines" and "megavoltage machines", said "most" other centres were in Asunción, and dated the reading 11 November (Second accuracy pass; IAEA DIRAC public equipment feed, raw JSON fetched 16 November 2026, six rows for Paraguay) · Now "11 linear accelerators in six centres", no cobalt-60 unit, three of six centres with brachytherapy (two high-dose-rate iridium-192 units, one high-dose-rate cobalt-60), centre names as the directory spells them, three of the other five in Asunción, entries last updated 2026
  • 2026-11-16 · Paraguay country page: The cancer fund card said "a quarter of a tobacco tax" goes to the fund and gave "40% of a health allocation from the FONACIDE public investment fund" (also in the Ministry of Health record) (Second accuracy pass; Law 6266 of 2018, article 23, full text on the Congress library site) · Now a quarter of a share of the tobacco tax set by an earlier law (25% of the participation rate in article 21(b) of Law 5538/15), and 40% of the contribution that FONACIDE and the fund for excellence in education and research make to the national health fund
  • 2026-11-16 · Paraguay country page: The gap card said "Paraguay screens for cervical cancer" with no source, and described the April 2026 imPACT team as "IAEA, PAHO and WHO reviewers" coordinated by PRONAC (Second accuracy pass; INCAN guidelines page and PAHO's release of 25 April 2026, raw HTML text) · Screening sentence reworded to what the sources show (an HPV and Pap study, a 2022 national guideline, no coverage figure); the review is now an IAEA-led team with PAHO/WHO technical support, coordinated by the Ministry with PRONAC's director
